articles.title: Documenting a Missing Item in an OrientDig Delivery
articles.description: Build a parcel-to-item record with packaging photos, order details and weights for a post-delivery support request.

sections.heading: Pause before throwing out the packaging
paragraphs: If a parcel arrives visibly torn or unusually light, preserve the condition in which it arrived. OrientDig's after-sales guide asks for photographic evidence and specifically calls for a weight picture before opening when the received weight is disputed. Photograph the whole parcel on a scale if one is available, keeping the unit visible. Capture damaged areas and the shipping label privately. Avoid altering the packaging until you have recorded the issue as clearly as possible.

sections.heading: Reconcile the actual parcel manifest
paragraphs: A purchase may be missing from this box because it was never assigned to it. Open the submitted parcel and list the item IDs and quantities included. Compare them with what you unpacked, including small items inside another product's box or wrapping. Mark each line present, missing or still uncertain. If two similar accessories were purchased from different sellers, identify which seller order is missing rather than reporting an unqualified count.

sections.heading: Choose photos that answer separate questions
paragraphs: A wide view can show all received items together. A close view can show a torn seal, wrong size label or damaged area. A photo of the interior packing can connect the condition of the goods to the condition of the parcel. OrientDig's published evidence guide distinguishes missing, stained, damaged and wrong-style cases. Select the pictures that substantiate your own issue. Keep originals so you can provide an uncropped image if a support reviewer needs more context.

sections.heading: File one clear account of the issue
paragraphs: Provide the parcel number, missing order number, ordered quantity, received quantity and delivery time. State the result you want investigated. The published after-sales page gives a 72-hour contact period for missing, damaged or defective goods after receipt, so contact support promptly and check current terms on your order. Keep the case reference and any requested follow-up together. When additional evidence arrives, add it to the same record so the sequence remains understandable.

sections.heading: Map the seller order to the parcel you received
paragraphs: Start with the delivery label and international parcel number. Open that parcel's manifest and identify each warehouse item assigned to it. A buyer may have paid for one cart, received several domestic packages and submitted more than one international box. A missing item from the whole shopping trip may be correctly absent from the particular parcel you are opening. Check whether another item still shows in storage, is in a second parcel or was refunded before attributing a shortage to packing or transit.

Next compare the manifest with physical pieces. A seller option described as a set can complicate the count: one warehouse item may contain three components, or a photograph of three components may correspond to only one selected accessory. Return to the original confirmed variant and package contents. Only once you know what should have been in the parcel can you describe what is actually missing. This distinction can radically change which team or seller should examine the evidence.

sections.heading: Build a photo sequence with an understandable scale
paragraphs: Begin with the full parcel and any visible damage. Include wider views that show where a tear or crushed corner sits relative to the box, then take closer images without losing the originals. If there is an available scale, place the parcel on it securely and make the reading and units visible. A blurry crop of a number cannot show whether it refers to this parcel, and a photograph taken after removing packing serves a different evidential purpose. Record which step each image represents.

Once opened, photograph the internal packing and items as found before separating everything for counting. Then lay out the received pieces in a way that makes identification possible. Two identical black pouches can look like one if stacked. A close-up of an option tag may connect a visually similar item to the correct seller order. Keep the shipping label and personal details for private submission only; a public discussion rarely needs your address or tracking identifier.

sections.heading: Handle an apparent weight discrepancy correctly
paragraphs: Suppose the warehouse record and the home scale differ slightly. Before treating that as proof of missing goods, verify that the two values represent the same thing. A billed weight can include a route calculation based on volume, while a home scale measures mass. An estimated submission weight can also differ from the finished parcel. Compare actual physical measurements in matching units when they are available. Keep the box and packing material in the comparison, and state whether your number was recorded before or after opening.

A substantial discrepancy may support further investigation without independently identifying where an item went missing. A correct-looking weight also does not prove every piece is present; similar items can weigh almost the same. Use the weight as one line of evidence alongside the manifest, warehouse photographs and received contents. When you contact support, provide the exact values and their sources rather than summarizing the issue as a claim that the carrier definitely removed something.

sections.heading: Choose evidence for a variant error or visible damage
paragraphs: If every piece is present but one has the wrong size, the evidence changes. Photograph the size marking and provide the original order selection. A garment that fits differently from expected and a garment labeled with a different size are two distinct observations. For a wrong style, compare the overall appearance with the confirmed item and identify a concrete difference such as the closure, pocket layout or model label. For damage, include a close view and an overall image identifying the affected item.

Preserve original tags, accessories and packaging while the case is being reviewed. If there appears to be liquid damage, note visible staining or wet packing as observed while avoiding unsupported conclusions about where the problem began. If repair or cleaning would change the evidence, document the condition first and ask the platform what it needs before acting. The goal is to create a record another person can evaluate without having been in the room when you opened the delivery.

sections.heading: Write the support request around one discrepancy
paragraphs: A useful missing-item message might read: “Parcel P includes item W on its manifest. The order confirms two units. I received one unit and have attached the parcel overview, packing and received contents. The sealed parcel weight was recorded in the attached image. Please check the packing and dispatch record for the second unit.” Replace the example identifiers and statements only with details you can actually support. If you could not weigh the unopened parcel, say so and supply the evidence you do have.

Contact the relevant support channel promptly and retain the case reference. If the agent requests additional images, keep them in the same case when possible and label any photographs taken after the original unpacking. Record the proposed resolution and any next deadline. If only part of a set is affected, clarify whether the proposed replacement or refund concerns that component or the whole item. A careful record protects both the time-sensitive claim and your ability to understand its eventual outcome.

sections.heading: Keep unresolved facts clearly labeled
paragraphs: If you did not take an unopened weight or the outer packaging has already been discarded, explain which evidence is unavailable and which records remain. The purchase confirmation, manifest, original warehouse images and photographs of the delivered goods can still help distinguish an omitted item from an incorrect seller option. Avoid recreating a staged unpacking image and presenting it as a contemporaneous photograph. A later layout of received contents can be useful when its timing is clear. The most credible claim is a straightforward account of what you found, what you documented and which missing detail you are asking the platform to investigate.

sources.title: OrientDig order and parcel status glossary

faq.q: Which seller links can I paste directly into OrientDig?
faq.a: The shopping guide lists product links from Taobao, Tmall, Weidian and 1688. Open the individual listing and verify the imported option before checkout.

faq.q: Can I order from a Yupoo album?
faq.a: OrientDig describes DIY ordering for sources such as Yupoo. Supply the specific model, source page, option and quantity so the agent can identify what to buy.

faq.q: How should I crop a picture for OrientDig image search?
faq.a: Keep one product prominent against a relatively plain background. Preserve distinguishing details such as the closure or profile, then verify the options on the result page.

faq.q: Can I buy a single unit from a 1688 listing?
faq.a: Check the seller's minimum and selling unit. Some sellers require more than one unit or pack, and the displayed price can depend on quantity.

faq.q: What does Purchased mean on an order?
faq.a: OrientDig has bought the item from the seller. This status precedes the seller's delivery to the warehouse.

faq.q: Where is my order when it shows Shipped (Local)?
faq.a: The seller has sent it on the domestic leg toward OrientDig. International shipment requires a separate parcel after warehouse processing.

faq.q: Why does an item show Received but remain unavailable to ship?
faq.a: Received is the warehouse arrival stage. Inspection, weighing and stock-in can still be pending.

faq.q: How does Stock arrived differ from Stored in warehouse?
faq.a: Stock arrived means inspection and weighing have been completed. Stored in warehouse means the item has been put into storage and can be considered for parcel submission.

faq.q: Why did my paid order enter Clear Balance?
faq.a: The glossary uses this status when the actual purchase amount exceeds the original payment. Review the order details and any message explaining the difference.

faq.q: Do standard QC pictures include a tape measurement?
faq.a: A specific measurement may require a detailed photograph. Identify the item, dimension, endpoints and units in the request.

faq.q: Can I ask for a blurry standard photograph to be taken again?
faq.a: OrientDig's photo guidance describes a free retake for unclear standard images. Reference the particular photo and explain which visible detail is unreadable.

faq.q: Does standard QC test an electronic device?
faq.a: The published inspection scope limits electronic and digital product checks to appearance. A warehouse image does not establish that the device powers on.

faq.q: When does the no-reason return clock start?
faq.a: The published terms for eligible items use the Stored in warehouse status and specify 120 hours. Check the order's deadline and submit promptly.

faq.q: Who approves a no-reason return?
faq.a: The agent can negotiate with the seller. Seller eligibility, resale condition and the applicable deadline affect the outcome.

faq.q: Can I see the weight before submitting the parcel?
faq.a: OrientDig lists rehearsal packing as an optional service. Specify the exact stored items and packing requirements, and check the terms before purchase.

faq.q: What is estimated billing weight?
faq.a: At submission the platform estimates outer packaging using stored item weights. The packed and measured parcel can differ.

faq.q: Can a light parcel be billed on volume?
faq.a: Yes, if the selected line uses dimensional charging and its calculated volumetric weight exceeds its actual weight. Check the specific route rule.

faq.q: What does Packaging Completed tell me?
faq.a: The parcel has been packed and is awaiting courier pickup. The glossary marks courier collection separately.

faq.q: Why might collection move to a later day?
faq.a: The dispatch guide notes that carrier pickup schedules, weekends and public holidays can affect when a packed parcel leaves.

faq.q: What should I photograph if the delivered weight seems wrong?
faq.a: OrientDig's evidence guide asks for a picture of the parcel being weighed before opening. Preserve the packaging and the parcel reference.

faq.q: What should I include when an item is missing after delivery?
faq.a: Identify the parcel and missing order, compare the manifest with what arrived, and supply photos of the received goods and packaging. Contact after-sales promptly.
